title: Dressings, Special Wounds, Crush and Blast Injuries

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already dress wounds, apply tourniquets and save amputated parts. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Pick the right dressing for the neck, chest, abdomen and limbs
  2. Manage impaled objects and amputations, and choose safe pain relief
  3. Anticipate crush syndrome and blast injuries, within BC scope

Textbook: Chapter 22, PDF pages 1852–1897
slides.say: Welcome back. Last lesson was about recognizing wounds; today is about treating them. As an EMR you already dress and bandage, apply tourniquets, and preserve amputated parts, so we'll move quickly through the basics and focus on decisions. Which dressing does each body part need, and why? How do you handle an impaled object or a torn flap? Which pain medicine is safe for a bleeding patient? Then two topics where the PCP must think ahead: crush syndrome, where the danger starts when the weight comes off, and blast injuries, where the worst damage may not show at first.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。上节课讲怎么认伤口，今天讲怎么处理。作为 EMR，你已经会包扎、上止血带、保存离断肢体，所以基础部分我们快速带过，重点放在决策上：每个部位该用什么敷料，为什么？刺入物和撕开的皮瓣怎么处理？出血的病人用什么止痛药才安全？然后是两个 PCP 必须提前想到的话题：挤压综合征，危险是从压着的重物搬开那一刻开始的；还有爆炸伤，最严重的损伤一开始可能看不出来。

slides.title: Dressings and bandages: the basics
slides.body:
• Dressing touches the wound; bandage holds it in place
  • Sterile dressing first, then bulky layers to soak up blood
  • Occlusive for the neck and chest; most others non-occlusive
  • Soaked through? Add layers; never pull off the first one
  • Irrigate with sterile water or saline, not peroxide or alcohol
  • Check pulse, motor, sensation before and after bandaging a limb
slides.say: A quick refresher. The dressing touches the wound and helps stop bleeding; the bandage holds the dressing in place. Put a sterile dressing on first, then bulky layers to soak up blood. Occlusive, or airtight, dressings are for the neck and chest; most other wounds get non-occlusive ones. If blood soaks through, add more layers on top. Never pull off the first dressing, because you'll tear away the clot. Rinse dirty wounds with sterile water or saline, and tell patients not to use hydrogen peroxide or alcohol, which damage tissue. And check pulse, movement, and sensation before and after you bandage a limb, because a tight bandage can cut off blood flow.
slides.sayZh: 快速复习一下。敷料直接贴在伤口上，帮助止血；绷带把敷料固定住。先放无菌敷料，再叠厚层吸血。封闭敷料，也就是不透气的敷料，用于颈部和胸部；其他大多数伤口用非封闭敷料。血渗透了，就在上面加层，绝不要揭掉第一层，否则会把血凝块一起撕掉。脏的伤口用无菌水或生理盐水冲洗，并告诉病人不要用双氧水或酒精，它们会损伤组织。包扎肢体前后都要检查脉搏、运动和感觉，因为绷带太紧会阻断血流。

slides.title: Big closed injuries: PRICED
slides.body:
• Protect: splint the part
  • Rest it
  • Ice, with a damp cloth between ice and skin
  • Compress: by hand, then an air splint
  • Elevate above the heart
  • Drugs: analgesia, where authorized

BC: apply cold only if distal circulation is not impaired.
slides.say: Small bruises need nothing special, but a large closed injury can bleed a lot under the skin and swell enough to cause trouble. The book uses PRICED. Protect the part with a splint. Rest it. Ice it, with a damp cloth between the ice and the skin. Compress it, first by hand, then with an air splint. Elevate it above the heart. And D is for drugs, meaning pain medication where you're authorized; the book warns that pain is often undertreated. For the BC exam, remember the Wound Care rule: apply cold only if the circulation beyond the injury isn't impaired.
slides.sayZh: 小的瘀伤不需要特别处理，但大面积闭合伤可能在皮下大量出血，肿到引起问题。书里用 PRICED：P 是保护，用夹板固定；R 是休息；I 是冰敷，冰和皮肤之间垫一条湿毛巾；C 是加压，先用手，再用充气夹板；E 是抬高到心脏以上；D 是药物，也就是在授权范围内给止痛药，书里提醒疼痛常常被处理不足。BC 考试要记住伤口处理流程的规定：只有伤处远端循环没有受损，才能冷敷。

slides.title: Pain relief: choosing from the BC list
slides.body:
BC optionWatch for
Acetaminophenliver disease; a dose in the last 4 h
Ibuprofennot with anticoagulants, active GI bleed, pregnancy
Entonoxnot with pneumothorax, air embolism, altered LOC
Methoxyfluranenot under 18, head injury, decreased LOC

The book's morphine, fentanyl and ketamine are not on the BC licensing exam. BCEHS: opioids are ACP; a PCP gives IN ketamine only with Flight Training, an endorsement and a consult.
slides.say: The Wound Care protocol says to give analgesia when appropriate. The book lists morphine, fentanyl, and ketamine, but none of those are on the BC licensing exam. In BCEHS, morphine and fentanyl are ACP drugs, and a PCP gives intranasal ketamine only with flight training, an endorsement, and a required consult. Your exam options come from the BC list, and each has traps. Acetaminophen: not with serious liver disease, or if a dose was taken in the last four hours. Ibuprofen: not with blood thinners, active stomach bleeding, or pregnancy; the book also avoids anti-inflammatories in bleeding patients because they interfere with clotting. Entonox: not with a pneumothorax, an air embolism, or altered consciousness. Methoxyflurane: not under eighteen, or with a head injury or decreased consciousness.
slides.sayZh: 伤口处理流程说，适当时要给镇痛。书里列了吗啡、芬太尼和氯胺酮，但执照考试不考这些。在 BCEHS，吗啡和芬太尼是 ACP 用药；PCP 要完成飞行培训（Flight Training）、取得授权并经强制咨询，才能给鼻内氯胺酮。考试时你的选择来自 BC 药物清单，每一种都有陷阱。对乙酰氨基酚：严重肝病不用，过去四小时内已服过也不用。布洛芬：用抗凝药、活动性消化道出血或怀孕时不用；书里也提醒出血病人避免消炎止痛药，因为它们干扰凝血。笑气：有气胸、空气栓塞或意识改变时不用。甲氧氟烷：未满十八岁、有颅脑外伤或意识下降时不用。

slides.q: A 68-year-old on apixaban has a deep forearm laceration, now bandaged with the bleeding controlled. He is alert, vital signs stable, pain 7/10. Which option should you avoid?
options: A cold pack over the dressing, if distal circulation is intact
slides.say: Let's check. A sixty-eight-year-old on apixaban has a deep forearm laceration, now bandaged with the bleeding controlled. He's alert, his vital signs are stable, and he rates his pain seven out of ten. Which option should you avoid? A, acetaminophen by mouth. B, ibuprofen by mouth. C, Entonox. D, a cold pack over the dressing, if the distal circulation is intact. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 检查一下。一位六十八岁、正在服阿哌沙班的男性，前臂有很深的裂伤，已包扎、出血已控制。他神志清醒、生命体征稳定，疼痛评分十分之七。哪个选项应该避免？A 口服对乙酰氨基酚；B 口服布洛芬；C 笑气；D 远端循环正常时，在敷料外冷敷。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Apixaban is an anticoagulant, and BC lists anticoagulant use as a contraindication to ibuprofen. The book also avoids anti-inflammatories in bleeding patients because they interfere with clotting. A is reasonable if he has no liver disease and hasn't taken any in the last four hours. C is fine for an alert patient with an isolated limb wound. D is allowed by the Wound Care protocol when the distal circulation is intact.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。阿哌沙班是抗凝药，BC 把正在用抗凝药列为布洛芬的禁忌证。书里也提醒出血病人避免消炎止痛药，因为它们干扰凝血。A 是合理的，只要他没有肝病、过去四小时没服过；C 适用于神志清醒、单纯肢体伤口的病人；D 在远端循环正常时，伤口处理流程是允许的。

slides.title: Impaled objects: leave them in
slides.body:
• Leave it in: removing it can start uncontrolled bleeding
  • Pressure around the object, never on it
  • Bulky dressings to stabilize; splint a limb; shorten only if huge
  • Eye: stacked gauze, a cup over it, cover both eyes
  • BC exception: it's impairing the airway
slides.say: Impaled objects stay in place. The object may be plugging a torn vessel, so pulling it out can start bleeding you can't control, and moving it damages more tissue inside. Control bleeding with pressure around the object, never on it. Stabilize it with bulky dressings, splint a limb, and don't cut it shorter unless it's huge, like a fence post. For an object in the eye, stack gauze pads cut to fit around it, place a paper cup over it, and cover both eyes, because the eyes move together. In BC, the exception is an object that's impairing the airway. The book also allows removal if it blocks CPR.
slides.sayZh: 刺入物要留在原位。它可能正堵着一根破裂的血管，拔出来可能引发无法控制的出血，晃动它还会伤到更多深部组织。止血要压在异物周围，绝不压在异物上。用厚敷料固定，肢体再加夹板；除非特别大，比如插进胸口的篱笆桩，否则不要截短。眼内刺入物：把剪开的纱布垫叠起来围住它，上面扣一个纸杯，并且双眼都要盖上，因为两只眼睛会一起转动。在 BC，例外是异物妨碍气道。书里还允许在它妨碍心肺复苏时取出。

slides.title: Avulsions and amputated parts
slides.body:
• Flap: rinse, fold it back untwisted, dry sterile pressure dressing
  • Never remove a skin flap, whatever its size

BC: Preservation of Amputated Parts

  1. Rinse with cool sterile water
  2. Wrap loosely in saline-moistened sterile gauze
  3. Plastic bag, kept cool in a protective container
  4. Transport it with the patient

Never warm it, never put it in water, never directly on ice, never dry ice.
slides.say: For a partial avulsion, rinse the area, fold the flap gently back into its normal position, making sure the base isn't twisted, and hold it with a dry, sterile pressure dressing. Never remove a flap, whatever its size. For an amputated part, BC has a set procedure. Rinse it with cool sterile water, wrap it loosely in saline-moistened sterile gauze, put it in a plastic bag, keep it cool in a protective container, and transport it with the patient. Then four nevers: never warm it, never put it in water, never place it directly on ice, which can freeze it, and never use dry ice.
slides.sayZh: 部分撕脱伤：冲洗伤处，把皮瓣轻轻折回正常位置，确认根部没有扭转，再用干燥的无菌加压敷料固定。皮瓣不管多大都绝不能剪掉。离断的肢体，BC 有固定流程：用凉的无菌水冲洗，用生理盐水浸湿的无菌纱布松松包好，装进塑料袋，放在保护性容器里保持低温，和病人一起转运。还有四个「绝不」：绝不加温，绝不泡在水里，绝不直接放在冰上，因为会冻伤，绝不用干冰。

slides.title: Dressing specific sites
slides.body:
SiteDo this
Scalpdirect pressure; skull fracture → press around the edges
Earcover loosely; never plug the canal
Neckfully occlusive, all four sides; press one side only
Chest, upper abdomenthree-sided occlusive or chest seal
Eviscerationmoist sterile dressing + occlusive layer; don't push back
Handposition of function, gauze roll in the palm
slides.say: Each site has its own rule. Scalp wounds bleed heavily, but the skull underneath makes direct pressure work well; if you feel a skull fracture, press around the edges. For the ear, cover it loosely and never plug the canal, because the fluid may contain cerebrospinal fluid. Neck wounds need a dressing sealed on all four sides, so air can't be sucked into a vein. Press backward, away from the airway, and never on both sides at once. Chest and upper abdominal wounds get a three-sided seal instead. For an evisceration, use a moist sterile dressing plus an occlusive layer, and never push the organs back.
slides.sayZh: 每个部位都有自己的规则。头皮伤出血多，但下面有颅骨，直接压迫效果很好；如果摸到颅骨骨折，就压在骨折周边。耳朵：松松地盖住，绝不堵耳道，因为流出的液体可能含脑脊液。颈部伤口要用四边全封的敷料，防止空气被吸进静脉；压迫时往后压，远离气道，而且绝不两侧同时压。胸部和上腹部伤口则用三边封闭。内脏脱出要用湿的无菌敷料再加一层封闭层，绝不把脏器塞回去。

slides.title: Crush syndrome: danger after rescue
slides.body:
Trapped > 4 hours→Muscle breaks down→Weight lifted: toxins flood in
  • Potassium → arrhythmia, sudden arrest ("smiling death")
  • Myoglobin and acid → kidney failure
  • Early killers: hypovolemia and high potassium
  • Book: IV fluid before the release; normal saline, not Ringer's
  • Scene safety first: collapse, technical rescue, second devices
slides.say: Crush syndrome is one of the few times the danger starts after the rescue. When a limb is trapped for more than four hours, the crushed muscle breaks down and releases potassium, acid, and myoglobin, but the weight keeps those toxins locked in. When the object is lifted, they flood the circulation. The potassium can stop the heart within moments; that's the smiling death, a patient chatting with rescuers who suddenly arrests. Myoglobin and acid damage the kidneys. The early killers are low volume and high potassium. So the book starts IV fluid before the release, using normal saline, because Ringer's lactate contains potassium. And scene safety still comes first.
slides.sayZh: 挤压综合征是少数「救出来之后才危险」的情况之一。肢体被压超过四小时，压坏的肌肉分解，释放出钾、酸和肌红蛋白，但重物把这些毒素锁在局部。重物一搬开，它们就涌进全身循环。钾可以在片刻之间让心脏停跳，这就是「微笑死亡」：病人还在和救援人员聊天，突然心脏骤停。肌红蛋白和酸会损伤肾脏。早期的杀手是低血容量和高血钾。所以书里在解压之前就开始静脉补液，用生理盐水，因为乳酸林格液含钾。当然，现场安全仍然第一。

slides.q: A worker's thigh has been pinned under a concrete slab for 6 hours. He is alert and talking. The rescue team is ready to lift. You are the PCP. What is the priority before the lift?
options: Lift right away; every minute trapped makes it worse
Start IV access and run normal saline before the release; be ready for arrhythmia or arrest
Run Ringer's lactate, because it is closer to body fluid
Give inhaled salbutamol to lower his potassium
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A worker's thigh has been pinned under a concrete slab for six hours. He's alert and talking, and the rescue team is ready to lift. What's your priority before the lift? A, lift right away, because every minute trapped makes it worse. B, start IV access and run normal saline before the release, and be ready for arrhythmia or arrest. C, run Ringer's lactate, because it's closer to body fluid. D, give inhaled salbutamol to lower his potassium. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名工人的大腿被混凝土板压了六个小时，神志清醒、能说话，救援队准备吊起重物。吊起之前你的首要任务是什么？A 马上吊，被压每多一分钟就更糟；B 解压前建立静脉通路、输注生理盐水，并准备好应对心律失常或心脏骤停；C 输乳酸林格液，因为它更接近体液；D 吸入沙丁胺醇来降血钾。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. After more than four hours of entrapment, the release can flood the body with potassium and leave the patient hypovolemic, so the book starts fluid before the lift and prepares for cardiac arrest. A risks the smiling death. C is wrong because Ringer's lactate contains potassium. D is not on the licensing exam: the exam lists salbutamol for bronchospasm, not for high potassium. In BCEHS practice, a PCP may give salbutamol for suspected hyperkalemia, or high potassium, in a crush injury, but only after a required CliniCall consultation, and fluid still comes first.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。被压超过四小时，一解压，大量的钾会涌进全身，病人还会出现低血容量，所以书里在吊起之前就开始补液，并做好心脏骤停的准备。A 可能导致「微笑死亡」；C 错在乳酸林格液含钾；D 不在执照考试范围内：考纲里沙丁胺醇用于支气管痉挛，不是用来降血钾的。在 BCEHS 实务中，PCP 可以对挤压伤中疑似高钾血症的病人给沙丁胺醇，但必须先咨询 CliniCall，而且补液仍然优先。

slides.title: Blast injuries: five levels
slides.body:
LevelCauseInjury
Primarypressure waveears, lungs, bowel
Secondaryflying debrispenetrating and blunt wounds
Tertiarybody thrownimpact with ground or walls
Quaternaryeverything elseburns, crush, entrapment
Quinaryadded contaminantschemical, biological, radioactive

Lung and bowel injuries can show up late: reassess often.
slides.say: Blast injuries come in five levels. Primary injuries come from the pressure wave, which damages air-filled organs: the ears, the lungs, and the bowel. Secondary injuries come from flying debris like glass and nails. Tertiary injuries happen when the person is thrown against the ground or a wall. Quaternary covers everything else, such as burns, crush, and entrapment. Quinary means chemical, biological, or radioactive material added to the bomb. If the blast was deliberate, think of a second device. And remember that lung and bowel injuries often appear late, so a patient who looks fine can get worse. Keep reassessing and listening to the lungs.
slides.sayZh: 爆炸伤分五级。一级来自压力波，伤的是含气的器官：耳朵、肺和肠道。二级来自飞散的碎片，比如玻璃和钉子。三级是人被抛起，撞到地面或墙上。四级包括其他一切，比如烧伤、挤压和被困。五级是炸弹里掺入的化学、生物或放射性物质。如果是蓄意爆炸，要想到第二个爆炸装置。还要记住，肺和肠道的损伤常常迟发，一开始看起来没事的病人也可能恶化，所以要不断复评、反复听肺。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: chest and abdominal wounds
slides.body:
BC Chest Trauma and Abdominal Injuries protocols

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Chest: three-sided seal or chest seal
  • Chest: watch for tension; relieve the seal if needed
  • Abdomen: control bleeding, limit movement, keep warm
  • Evisceration: moist sterile dressing + occlusive layer
  • Don't put organs back; position of comfort

PCP adds (en route)

  • Chest: vascular access if required
  • Abdomen: vascular access, correct hypoperfusion
  • Both: TXA if indicated
  • Hypovolemia protocol may start before BP drops if shock is expected
slides.say: Here's what changes for chest and abdominal wounds. Every licence level seals an open chest wound with a three-sided dressing or a chest seal, watches for tension, and relieves the seal if needed. For the abdomen, everyone controls bleeding, limits movement so clots aren't disturbed, keeps the patient warm, and covers eviscerated organs with a moist sterile dressing and an occlusive layer, without pushing them back. The PCP adds vascular access en route, correcting hypoperfusion in abdominal injuries, and TXA, tranexamic acid, when indicated. And for a crush or big wounds, remember that the hypovolemia protocol can start before the pressure drops, when the mechanism tells you shock is coming.
slides.sayZh: 看看胸部和腹部伤口有什么变化。所有执照级别都要：开放性胸伤用三边封闭敷料或胸部封贴封住，观察张力征象，必要时给封贴放气。腹部：控制出血、减少搬动以免冲掉血凝块、保暖；脱出的脏器用湿的无菌敷料加一层封闭层盖好，不塞回去。PCP 多做的是：途中开静脉，腹部伤要纠正低灌注，有指征时给 TXA，也就是氨甲环酸。对挤压伤或大面积伤口，记住：当受伤机制提示休克即将发生时，低血容量流程可以在血压掉之前就启动。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Tension: no needle decompression on the BC exam → relieve the seal
  • Lung sounds: at least 6 points front or back (book: 2 per side)
  • Opioids, ketamine: not on the exam (BCEHS: opioids ACP; IN ketamine: endorsed PCP)
  • Crush drugs (insulin, D50W, calcium…): not on the exam list; no IO procedure in the exam guidelines
  • BC's only IV dextrose is D10W
  • Amputated part: rinse with cool sterile water (book: saline)
slides.say: Now the book-versus-BC differences. The book uses needle decompression for tension from a chest wound or a blast; the BC exam has no needle decompression, so you relieve the seal and transport. The book listens at two spots on each side of the chest; BC wants at least six points on the front or six on the back. The book's opioids and ketamine aren't on the licensing exam; in BCEHS, opioids are ACP drugs, and only an endorsed PCP gives intranasal ketamine, after a consult. The book's crush treatments, like insulin, fifty percent dextrose, calcium, bicarbonate, and mannitol, are not on the BC exam drug list. The BC exam guidelines describe IV access only, with no procedure for an IO, or intraosseous, line. And BC's only IV dextrose is D10W, ten percent dextrose. Finally, BC rinses an amputated part with cool sterile water.
slides.sayZh: 现在看书和 BC 的不同。书上对胸部伤或爆炸导致的张力性气胸做针刺减压；BC 执照考试里没有针刺减压，你要给封贴放气并转运。书上每侧胸部听两个点；BC 要求前胸至少六个点或后背六个点。书里的阿片类药物和氯胺酮执照考试不考；在 BCEHS，阿片类是 ACP 用药，鼻内氯胺酮只有取得授权的 PCP 经咨询后才能给。书里治疗挤压综合征的胰岛素、百分之五十的葡萄糖、钙剂、碳酸氢钠、甘露醇，都不在 BC 考试药物清单上；BC 考纲只讲静脉通路，没有建立 IO 骨髓腔通路的操作；BC 唯一的静脉葡萄糖是 D10W，也就是百分之十的葡萄糖。最后，BC 用凉的无菌水冲洗离断肢体。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Crush: fluid before the release; be ready for sudden arrest
  • Crush: normal saline, not Ringer's lactate (it contains potassium)
  • Suspected pneumothorax or air embolism → no Entonox
  • Ibuprofen: not with anticoagulants or active bleeding
  • Tourniquet: mark "TK" and the time; don't loosen it for pain
  • Blast patients who look fine can crash: keep reassessing
slides.say: Now the PCP watch-outs for this lesson. In a crush trapped for hours, fluid goes in before the weight comes off, and you're ready for cardiac arrest the moment it lifts. Use normal saline, not Ringer's lactate, because Ringer's contains potassium. A suspected pneumothorax or air embolism rules out Entonox, so think of both with blast, chest, and neck wounds. Ibuprofen is out with anticoagulants or active bleeding. Mark a tourniquet with TK and the time, and don't loosen it just because it hurts; a working tourniquet does hurt. And a blast patient who looks fine can crash, so keep reassessing.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲这节课 PCP 要注意的地方。被压了几个小时的挤压伤，要在重物搬开之前补液，并在搬开那一刻做好心脏骤停的准备。用生理盐水，不用乳酸林格液，因为后者含钾。怀疑气胸或空气栓塞时不能用笑气，所以遇到爆炸伤、胸部伤和颈部伤都要想到这两点。用抗凝药或正在活动性出血时，不用布洛芬。止血带要标上 TK 和时间，不要因为病人喊痛就松开，有效的止血带本来就痛。看起来没事的爆炸伤病人也可能突然恶化，所以要不断复评。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Neck: seal 4 sides; chest: 3 sides; organs out: moist + occlusive
  2. Impaled objects stay in; amputated parts go cool and bagged, never on ice
  3. Crush > 4 hours: normal saline before the release; expect arrest

Next: Chapter 23, Burns
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: match the dressing to the site. Seal a neck wound on all four sides and a chest wound on three, and cover eviscerated organs with a moist sterile dressing plus an occlusive layer, never pushing them back. Two: impaled objects stay in unless they block the airway, and an amputated part is rinsed, wrapped in moist gauze, bagged, and kept cool, never directly on ice. Three: in a crush longer than four hours, normal saline goes in before the release, and you're ready for cardiac arrest. Next, Chapter twenty-three: burns. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，敷料要配合部位：颈部伤口四边全封，胸部伤口三边封，脱出的脏器用湿的无菌敷料加封闭层盖好，绝不塞回去。二，刺入物除非堵住气道，否则留在原位；离断肢体要冲洗、用湿纱布包好、装袋、保持低温，绝不直接放在冰上。三，被压超过四小时的挤压伤，解压前先输生理盐水，并做好心脏骤停的准备。下一章是第二十三章：烧伤。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
